items.title: OM review: Dhanush and Mammootty team up for a spy thriller that loses the plot halfway
items.summary: OM: Operation Mole (Tamil) In 2015, the Andhra Pradesh Red Sanders Anti-Smuggling Task Force opened fire on 20 Tamil labourers in Seshachalam. The cops claimed it was self-defence. The men’s families and human rights organisations have maintained that these were unprovoked extrajudicial murders. At the time, police said they stumbled on the men attempting to cut down red sanders trees for smuggling. But allegations only grew that the so-called ‘encounter’ was staged. No clear answers have emerged since. Their deaths are the heart of Director Rajkumar Periasamy’s OM: Operation Mole. Dhanush plays Palani alias Thirukumaran, a special operative trained in infiltrating organised crime networks. He’s soon sent undercover to a Red Sanders smuggling operation. Here, Palani meets Karthikeyan (Mammootty), who oversees the Chennai arm of the network. Karthikeyan, like Mammootty in the 1991 Thalapathi , is a gangster well-loved by his neighbourhood. He has his own codes and is mindful of who is most vulnerable to the ongoing feud between smugglers and cops. He values loyalty above all else. items.title: AP raises semiconductor incentives, offers up to 80% support for silicon fabs
items.summary: The Andhra Pradesh government has amended its Semiconductor and Display Fab Policy 4.0 to align it with the second phase of the India Semiconductor Mission (ISM 2.0), offering state incentives that match Union support for several project categories. The amendment, notified through G.O.Ms.No.87 on November 16, provides combined Union and State incentives of up to 80% of eligible capital costs for silicon fabrication projects, with each government contributing 40%. Compound semiconductor, photonics, sensor, discrete semiconductor and display fabrication projects, as well as advanced packaging units, will be eligible for combined support of up to 70%. Legacy packaging units can receive up to 50%, according to the policy details. For assembly, testing, marking and packaging (ATMP) and outsourced semiconductor assembly and test (OSAT) facilities, Andhra Pradesh will match 100% of the Centre’s capital support. The state will also provide a deployment-linked incentive of 4.5% of net sales, in addition to the Union’s 9%, taking the combined incentive to 13.5%. This support will be capped at Rs 45 crore per application and Rs 180 crore per company. For semiconductor machinery and materials
